text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- The World Jewish Congress accused the Swiss National Bank of having earned over three billion dollars from deals with Nazi gold.
- The Federal Trade Commission gave pharmaceutical giants Ciba and Sandoz permission to merge.
- Switzerland topped the list of European countries with economic freedom in a study published by the Heritage Foundation in cooperation with the Wall Street Journal.
- The Basle Insurance Group announced its intention to separate from its subsidiaries in Italy, France and Spain.
- Two Finnish paper companies, Metsa-Serla and Myllykoski, are buying the Biber Group, which accumulated a loss of 1.3 billion Swiss francs from 1987 to 1996, for 185 million francs.
- Switzerland is supporting the Ukraine government's shutting down of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant with 20 million Swiss francs.
- Bakery group Manuel, with four branches in Lausanne and Geneva, is restructuring after several years of losses.
